scope: game addons: the meta-systems around the arcade (progression, social and competitive layers, spectating and sharing, practice and learning, personal arcade statistics, seasonal structures, coaching, cross-game systems, arcade quality of life) plus extensions to the wheel, the daily loop and the heist mechanic

ideas.title: Per-game mastery tracks
ideas.body: Each of the 13 games gets its own mastery level, computed from that member's game_rounds rows for that game - rounds played, rounds won, best payout, and a shrinking weight on the oldest rounds so mastery reflects current form. The mastery level and title (Novice, Adept, Veteran, Master) render on the game tile in the hub and on a per-game mastery board beside the existing global one, and a mastery-up writes the usual feed entry and changelog row. This is distinct from the global XP level and the coverage-based Curator Level, both of which ignore which games a member actually plays. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: weighting by bet size turns mastery into a wealth score, so the formula must count rounds and outcomes rather than coins wagered, or a single whale outranks genuine players.
ideas.why: The site has 13 games but no way to show that someone is genuinely good at one of them rather than merely high level.

ideas.title: Badge knowledge profile
ideas.body: The quiz and memory games already know which catalog badges a member answered correctly, so store that as a private knowledge profile per user (badge_id, correct, seen_at) and surface 'you can name 243 of 476 badges' with the categories you are weakest in. The quiz then samples adaptively - roughly 70% from weak categories and 30% from everything - so the game stays learnable instead of cycling the same easy art, and a study list of the badges the member keeps missing links into the catalog. It uses only the existing catalog rows and the round results the quiz engine already returns. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: if the profile is public it becomes a published list of what a member does not know, so it must be private by default with an explicit opt-in to show a knowledge score.
ideas.why: The badge quiz is the one game whose difficulty could be personal, and the catalog already holds exactly the data to make it so.

ideas.title: Self-authored arcade contracts
ideas.body: Before playing, a member writes a contract from a closed vocabulary - 'win 5 rounds of Tower of Badges at a bet of 100 or more within 7 days' - escrowing a coin deposit; the contract stores its window and is evaluated by the same server-side predicate style the achievements already use. Completing it returns the deposit plus a bonus scaled by difficulty, letting it expire returns the deposit minus a small fee, and a 'contracts written / kept' count sits on the profile. This differs from the server-issued daily trials and the fixed 125 achievements because the player sets the terms and stakes coins on them. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: the clause vocabulary must be closed and validated server-side, or a member words an impossible clause, keeps the bonus, and the contract system mints coins.
ideas.why: Collectors already set their own goals in the catalog; giving the arcade the same self-directed structure turns play into a personal commitment.

ideas.title: Prestige track past level 100
ideas.body: Past level 100 the XP bar does not stop: total XP beyond the 254,900 cap converts into prestige stars (one per 50,000 XP), shown as a small laurel count beside the level badge and in place of an unbounded level number on the leaderboards. Prestige is display-only, cannot be bought, and the level badge keeps its Mythic theme at zero stars. It reads the XP already stored in user_progress, so no new data source is needed. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: if the star threshold is too low the top of the ladder flattens within a week, so the spacing should be set from the observed XP distribution of the current top 100 before launch.
ideas.why: The level ladder ends at 100, and the site's longest-running players need somewhere for the number to keep meaning something.

ideas.title: Level-gated game unlocks
ideas.body: The high-variance games (blackjack, roulette, coin-flip ladder) stay locked until a member reaches a configured level, and each locked tile shows the level required and a one-line reason to learn the slower games first. Gates come from the admin settings document, so the panel can move or drop a gate without a deploy, and a locked tile still links to the rules page while tracking stays open. Crossing a threshold writes a small 'new game unlocked' notification. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: gating a game players already spent coins on reads as punishment, so gates must apply only to accounts created after the feature ships or be announced ahead with a grace period.
ideas.why: New members meet 13 games at once with no ordering, and a staged unlock gives the arcade a shape without removing any game.

ideas.title: Persistent rivalry ledger
ideas.body: Two members declare a rivalry, and from then on every shared arena is scored into a persistent head-to-head record: rounds compared by net coins in the same game on the same day, heists between the pair, and wheel results, with wins, losses, biggest single margin and longest run. The rivalry card lives on both profiles behind a link only the pair can open, and either side can end it at any time. This is a standing record over time, unlike a duel's one-off best-of-three or the pairwise catalog compare. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: scoring must be computed from a cached daily aggregate rather than per page load, or the ledger runs a recompute over game_rounds and steal_attempts on every profile view.
ideas.why: Stealing and games already produce friction between members, and a rivalry ledger gives that friction a running score instead of a one-off event.

ideas.title: Spectator channel for public rounds
ideas.body: A member can switch 'broadcast my rounds' on for a session; the arcade then publishes each resolved round as a lightweight activity event whose id appears on a /watch page that polls or subscribes over SSE for the newest rounds of members currently broadcasting. Watchers see the game, the bet tier, win or loss and the payout, with the player's identity shown only if they opted into being named. This differs from a shared multiplayer table (where the watcher also plays) and from the site-wide activity feed (which includes everything). Effort: M. Risk if built badly: without a hard per-session expiry the broadcast flag stays on forever and private play becomes a permanent public log, and a stream keyed on user id leaks who is playing right now.
ideas.why: The arcade has no audience layer at all, and the big wins that make the feed are exactly the moments nobody can currently watch live.

ideas.title: Spectator side-bets on rounds
ideas.body: On a broadcast round a watcher places a small stake, capped well below the game's own maximum, on the next round's outcome before it resolves; the stake is escrowed server-side, settled when the round lands, and the watcher's net goes through the normal coin path. Bets void if the caster stops, and the caster earns a small rake so being watched is worth something. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: this is a pure-chance betting surface, so the cap, the per-watcher daily limit and the rake belong in the settings document rather than in code, and settlement must happen only after the round is committed server-side or a spectator can bet on a known result.
ideas.why: Watching is currently worth nothing and costs nothing; a capped stake plus a rake to the player turns spectators into participants.

ideas.title: Wanted board with restitution
ideas.body: From steal_attempts the site builds a rolling 'most wanted' board of thieves - successful heists, coins taken, distinct victims - and a robbed member can post a coin bounty that any other member claims by successfully robbing that thief within a fixed window. Claiming pays the bounty plus the stolen amount, and amounts below a floor are aggregated so small heists do not become a public shaming list. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a public board invites coordinated dogpiling on one account, so it needs a per-thief daily claim cap and must never expose the victim's identity without consent.
ideas.why: Stealing is the site's most social mechanic and currently leaves the victim with no legal way to respond.

ideas.title: Arcade Grand Prix circuit
ideas.body: A scheduled circuit runs one day per game; each day's rounds feed that day's points (payout above a floor plus a placement bonus) and the cumulative table crowns an all-rounder champion with a season trophy. Points come from game_rounds filtered to the day's game, so nothing new is collected, and a live circuit page shows today's game, the standings and the days remaining. It differs from the single-elimination weekly bracket and from the seasonal ladder reset because it measures breadth across all 13 games over a fixed schedule. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: one day per game overruns a weekly promise, so the schedule length must be a panel setting, and the scoring formula must stop one enormous lucky payout from deciding the whole circuit.
ideas.why: A badge catalog rewards breadth of collecting, and the arcade has no equivalent that rewards breadth of play.

ideas.title: Community strategy playbooks
ideas.body: Each game gets a guide page where members publish short, attributed strategies ('cash out Tower at floor 4 - the expected value peaks there'), versioned and votable with the top-rated one pinned. Guides are length-capped plain text with a report control, votes are one per member per guide, and every guide records the engine-constants revision it was written against so the page can mark it stale after a rules change. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: it is user text, so escaping and a report path are required from day one, and without the constants revision every balance change silently turns the top guide into bad advice.
ideas.why: Nothing on the site tells a new player how a game is actually played well, and the arcade's regulars already know.

ideas.title: Round share card
ideas.body: A dedicated OG route renders one round as a share card: the game, its badge-themed visual, bet, payout, net, and a footer linking to the verifiable round record. It appears as a 'share this round' action on the result panel and in the round tape, and the image is cached per round id like the other OG routes. The existing cards cover badges and profiles, not the one artifact a player actually wants to brag about. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: satori re-renders per crawler fetch, so the route must be immutable-cached on the round id and must not expose another member's round id to a logged-out visitor unless that round was explicitly published.
ideas.why: Big wins are the arcade's most shareable output and currently leave the site as a screenshot or nothing.

ideas.title: Hall of Fame record book
ideas.body: A nightly job reads game_rounds and steal_attempts to maintain an all-time record book: biggest single payout, longest coin-flip ladder, longest win streak, biggest heist, best day by net, longest wheel dry streak. Each record shows the holder, the value and the date it was set, with a 'beaten' entry when it falls; records live in their own small table so a holder keeps the title even after the underlying rows are pruned. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: recomputing extremes over a growing game_rounds table on every page load will not hold, so the nightly job must write a standing record and replace it only on a strictly better value.
ideas.why: Live leaderboards show who is ahead this week; a record book is the thing that makes an old result permanent.

ideas.title: Mistake drill from your misses
ideas.body: Quiz, memory and vault already know which question or tile a member got wrong, so a drill mode serves a short no-wager round built only from that member's recent misses, running the same engine and the same one-round-per-second limit. An item clears once answered correctly twice, and drill results pay only a small daily-capped XP trickle instead of coins. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a drill that pays like a real round is free money, so the XP must be capped per day and per drill and the drill set must be rebuilt from the misses rather than hoarded.
ideas.why: The skill games currently punish the same knowledge gap forever, and the misses are already recorded.

ideas.title: Coin-priced in-round hints
ideas.body: During a skill round a member can buy one hint through the normal server path: reveal a memory tile, remove two wrong quiz options, or show the vault's next digit, priced per game in the settings document and scaled to the current bet. The hint is consumed server-side in the same round, the round is flagged as hinted, and the payout is reduced by a fixed fraction so the option assists rather than pays. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: hints that leave the payout untouched make the skill games trivially profitable, so the payout reduction and the one-hint-per-round rule are the whole safety mechanism and must live in the engine, never the client.
ideas.why: The skill games have a hard wall for new players, and a priced hint converts frustration into a small, honest coin sink.

ideas.title: Bankroll coach bet suggestion
ideas.body: Before a round a single line suggests a stake for the member's stated goal - 'you hold 12,000 coins and a 30,000 target; a flat 1 to 2 percent stake survives typical variance, an all-in does not' - computed on the server from the balance, that game's payout distribution constants and its configured limits. The suggestion is never auto-applied and can be dismissed permanently from arcade preferences. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a suggestion that reads as financial advice invites blame when it loses, so it must be framed as a variance note with the arithmetic shown and must reference only the site's own coins.
ideas.why: The arcade has a strong pull toward all-in play and the payout maths needed to counter it is already in the engine.

ideas.title: Training-wheels loss rebate
ideas.body: For accounts below level 5, one lost round per day is refunded up to a fixed small cap, and the refund panel shows one sentence explaining the rule the round illustrates. The rebate is tracked as its own counter and expires forever at level 5. It is deliberately not a free-play mode: the coins are genuinely at risk and only the first daily loss comes back. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a rebate that can be farmed by betting the maximum on a high-variance game each day is a coin printer, so the cap must be a fixed amount rather than a share of the bet.
ideas.why: The first sessions decide whether a newcomer stays, and the existing arcade offers them nothing to soften the first losses.

ideas.title: Personal RTP and variance report
ideas.body: For each game a member has played, the report computes actual return (payout sum over bet sum), the expected return implied by the published payout distribution, the difference in standard deviations, and a hot or cold flag that always states the sample size. It is a computed layer over game_rounds and the engine constants, not another counter, and it plainly says when the sample is too small to mean anything. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a report that calls a normal swing an unlucky streak trains superstition, so the z-score must ship with its confidence band and the wording must never imply the games owe a member a correction.
ideas.why: The site publishes the odds, and the natural counterpart is showing each member what those odds actually did to their own coins.

ideas.title: In-game round tape
ideas.body: Inside each game panel a strip shows the last 20 rounds of that game for the member - bet, outcome, payout, net and a sparkline of running net - flagging any round that was hinted or insured. The rows are already in game_rounds; the tape is the per-round record the aggregate counters throw away. Selecting a row opens the round detail with its inputs and result payload. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: it must read only the signed-in member's rows, or a round that member published, or the tape becomes a window into other people's betting.
ideas.why: Players remember rounds, not totals, and the round rows exist but are never shown back to the person who played them.

ideas.title: Declared session with stop-loss lock
ideas.body: A member declares a session before entering the arcade - starting balance, a target and a stop-loss - and the arcade shows the session bar everywhere, locks play when either line is crossed, and holds a cooling-off screen until a configured time passes. The session is clocked from the round timestamps already recorded, and its summary (net, rounds, best round, minutes) is written to the member's arcade history. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a lock that clears on reload is theatre, so it must be enforced in the same server-side gate the rate limiter already sits in, with a cooldown the client cannot shorten.
ideas.why: The arcade has no brake at all, and a declared limit is the one that works because the player sets it themselves.

ideas.title: Personal bet-pattern profile
ideas.body: A segmentation view over a member's own rounds: win rate by bet bucket, by hour of day, by game, and by the streak they were on when they entered, plus a one-line playstyle label derived from those numbers with the inputs shown. The existing per-game stats are totals; this is the same rows cut differently, computed on demand with a bounded lookback window. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: slicing a few hundred rounds by hour produces confident-looking nonsense, so any bucket below a stated minimum sample must be hidden rather than reported as a finding.
ideas.why: Collectors can see how their catalog is shaped but not how their own play is shaped, and the rows to answer that are already stored.

ideas.title: Best-value game recommender
ideas.body: From the member's own rounds, the per-game XP rules and the configured bet bounds, the hub computes where that member's XP per coin and observed net are best right now - 'Tower of Badges has returned 0.6 XP per coin over 214 rounds; roulette has returned 0.2' - and shows one suggestion. It recommends a game rather than a stake, which keeps it separate from the bet coach. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a recommender that confidently points at a house-edge game encourages chasing, so it must report observed XP per coin and state plainly that coin expectation is negative.
ideas.why: Thirteen games with different value profiles and no guidance is a puzzle the site can answer from data it already has.

ideas.title: Seasonal arcade pass
ideas.body: Each season carries a pass bought with BadgesCoins, never cash, unlocking a two-track reward path: a free track everyone fills by playing, and a paid track with table themes, a season profile frame and scrip. Progress is season XP earned from rounds, heists and the wheel, tracked per pass and reset with the season, and the pass grants no coins or XP multipliers so it cannot feed the economy. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: a pass is the classic grind machine, so the path must be short and reachable in a few sessions, and the paid track must never accept real money or the addon becomes commerce.
ideas.why: Seasons reset the ladder and take everything with them; a pass is what makes a season leave something behind.

ideas.title: Weekly game mutators
ideas.body: Every week the panel picks one mutator that changes the rules of an existing game for everyone - double-or-nothing blackjack, slots that pay on two of a kind with a halved bet, a roulette green-zero bonus - announced on the hub with the affected game and reverted automatically at the week's end. A mutator is a small server-side override read from the settings document by the resolver the games already use, so it needs no new game code. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a mutator that improves expected value becomes a week-long farming route, so each one must be checked against the payout maths before it ships and the settings document must stay the only source so a bad one can be switched off mid-week.
ideas.why: The same 13 games every day is the arcade's biggest retention problem, and rule twists buy novelty without shipping new games.

ideas.title: Scheduled arcade nights
ideas.body: The panel schedules themed hours ('Slots Hour', 'Heist Hour') on a published calendar; during a night the featured game gets a raised maximum bet and its own hourly board, and finishing on that board pays a catalog-linked cosmetic. The schedule is a settings row, the boards are computed from game_rounds in the window, and the page shows the next three nights in the member's local time. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: hourly boards invite all-night botting, so the one-round-per-second limit stays in force and the board should reward placement rather than raw round count, or the winner is simply whoever stayed awake.
ideas.why: The arcade is always-on and never scheduled, so nothing gives members a reason to show up at the same time as each other.

ideas.title: Career trophy room
ideas.body: A profile section accumulates competitive results - Grand Prix placements, season championships, circuit wins, top reviewer marks - each as a dated trophy naming the event it came from, kept even after the season resets. It reads a small results table written when an event closes, so trophies survive both the seasonal reset and any pruning. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: trophy rows must be written only by the closing job, or a client can insert its own honours, and the room must not become a second leaderboard of badge counts.
ideas.why: Competitive results currently expire with the season, which makes winning something the site then forgets.

ideas.title: Post-round skill diagnostic
ideas.body: After a skill round that was lost, or that ended below a configured threshold, the result panel shows a short server-generated explanation of the decisive input - 'you called it at floor 6 with a 22 percent bust chance; cashing at floor 4 was the value line' - built from the recorded inputs and the same probability constants the engine used. It is generated for that round only, never stored as advice, and never shown for the luck games where no decision existed. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: an explanation that is wrong or post-hoc destroys trust, so only inputs with a known optimal line should produce a diagnostic and the rest must say there was no decision to review.
ideas.why: Skill games currently return a score and nothing else, so a loss teaches a player nothing about the next round.

ideas.title: Round review marketplace
ideas.body: A member requests a paid review of their last N rounds in one game, optionally naming a higher-mastery reviewer; the requester escrows coins, the reviewer writes a short structured critique of bet sizing, cash-out timing and mistake pattern from the round tape, and payment releases on submission with a dispute window. Reviewer reputation comes from reviews written and ratings received, and the work is a one-off audit rather than the ongoing pairing the mentorship idea describes. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: this is a marketplace for advice, so escrow, dispute handling and a volume cap are required, and a reviewer must never see rounds the requester did not explicitly share.
ideas.why: Mastery tracks will create exactly the kind of experts whose knowledge is worth paying for, and the round tape gives them something to read.

ideas.title: Cross-game parlay ticket
ideas.body: A member builds one ticket of two to four legs across different games - each leg a stated condition such as 'win a round of Higher or Lower' or 'survive floor 3 of Tower' - staking a single amount and taking a combined multiplier derived from the legs' published odds, with every leg to be played inside a fixed window. The engine resolves each leg through the normal round path and holds the ticket until it is settled or expires. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: a parlay compounds the house edge and invites ruin-chasing, so the leg count, the stake cap and the expiry must be tight and the multiplier must be computed from the constants rather than hand-set.
ideas.why: The 13 games are currently isolated from each other, and a ticket is the simplest way to make them reference one another.

ideas.title: Risk profiles per round
ideas.body: Before a round the member picks Conservative, Standard or Degenerate; the engine applies a defined tweak to that round's payout curve - Conservative pays more often and less, Degenerate pays rarely and large - with expected value held constant, and the chosen profile is stored on the round. The published-odds page gains a per-profile column so the choice is auditable against the same constants the engine reads. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: if the profiles do not conserve expected value one becomes strictly best and the others are decoration, so the constants must satisfy the identity and be verified in a test rather than eyeballed.
ideas.why: Every game offers one volatility, and the choice between steady and swingy is the thing players actually care about.

ideas.title: Arcade scrip currency
ideas.body: A second, non-purchasable currency is earned only by playing - a little per round, more for win streaks - and is spent on a second chance at a lost round, a bonus spin voucher, or arcade cosmetics. Scrip can never be converted into coins and is never granted for spending coins, so it rewards play without inflating the coin economy, and its balance is shown separately everywhere coins appear. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: scrip that converts to coins, directly or through a purchasable item, becomes a coin faucet, so the no-conversion rule must be enforced in the database, not only in application code.
ideas.why: A pure reward layer with no cash-out lets the arcade pay out generously for play while leaving the coin economy untouched.

ideas.title: Cross-game handoff streak
ideas.body: Winning a round unlocks a handoff: the next round played in a different game carries a small XP and scrip bonus, and the bonus grows as the chain moves through distinct games, resetting if the member repeats a game or loses. The chain state is per day, kept on the progress row, and drawn as a small counter in the arcade header. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: an escalating multiplier across games rewards speed over thought, so the bonus must cap at a low multiple and apply to XP and scrip only, never to payouts.
ideas.why: Nothing currently encourages a member to try a second game, and the cheapest fix is a reward for variety rather than a new game.

ideas.title: Auto-play with stop conditions
ideas.body: In the games with no per-round decision (slots, scratch, fixed-bet roulette) a member starts an auto-run of up to N rounds at a fixed stake with stop conditions - stop on a win above X, stop after Y losses, stop below balance Z - paced by the engine's one-round-per-second limit and always cancellable between rounds. Every round still goes through the normal server path, so the audit trail and rate limit are unchanged. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: auto-play is exactly where a bankroll disappears unattended, so every run must require a stop-loss, default to a low round cap, and stop on a server-side balance check rather than trusting the client.
ideas.why: The three decision-free games are pure repetition to click by hand, and the server already paces them.

ideas.title: Per-game keyboard hotkey maps
ideas.body: Each game gets a documented key map - number keys for a quiz answer, arrows for the vault, space to cash out, enter to bet the remembered amount - shown in a collapsible legend inside the panel and remembered per member. The keys drive the same controls the mouse does, so no new game logic is needed, and the legend ships through the localized messages. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: keys must not fire while a text field or modal has focus, or typing in an input plays rounds, so the handler belongs behind the existing modal focus trap.
ideas.why: Several of the 13 games are keyboard-shaped (quiz, memory, vault) and currently waste that by requiring a mouse.

ideas.title: Quick-bet rail with bet memory
ideas.body: A rail under the game controls offers halve, double, minimum, maximum and repeat-last-bet, with the last stake per game persisted on the progress row so returning to a game restores it. The rail reads the per-game bounds from the same settings the engine enforces, so it can never offer a stake the server would reject. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: an all-in button beside a double button is a misclick machine, so the maximum action must be capped below the true maximum and both must sit away from the play control.
ideas.why: Every round currently requires typing the same stake again, which is the most repeated interaction in the arcade.

ideas.title: Hold-to-confirm for large bets
ideas.body: Any stake above a per-member threshold, set in arcade preferences and defaulting to a fraction of the balance, must be confirmed by holding the play control for a moment while the amount and the possible loss are shown; below the threshold nothing changes. The threshold and the resulting confirmation are flagged on the round. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a confirmation that can be switched off entirely removes the protection from the people it exists for, so the threshold may be raised but not disabled below a floor.
ideas.why: A single misclick at the maximum bet can erase a session, and the arcade currently offers no friction at all on the largest action.

ideas.title: Personal arcade day boundary
ideas.body: The daily loop turns over at a fixed UTC time, which is invisible in the UI; this feature derives each member's own boundary from the timezone offset already stored with their analytics and shows 'your day ends in 3h - streak and spin still unclaimed' with a one-tap jump to whatever is outstanding. The boundary only changes what the interface displays and warns about; the server keeps its existing UTC gate so a day can never be claimed twice. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: if the local boundary ever feeds the claim gate it opens double-claiming across timezones, so display and enforcement must stay separate and the separation must be stated in the code.
ideas.why: Members lose streaks to a reset they cannot see, and the site already knows each visitor's timezone offset.

ideas.title: Streak-scaled wheel table
ideas.body: The daily wheel's prize table upgrades with the member's login streak: at 7, 30 and 100 days the low tiers are removed or doubled, visible on the wheel as the segments that fall away and stated on the page. It reads the existing streak counter and wheel slots, and each spin records which table version it used. This differs from a pity timer because the improvement comes from returning, not from a run of poor spins. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a streak multiplier compounds with the daily bonus, so the upgrade must favour the XP-heavy tiers and leave coin prizes flat or long streaks become the site's best coin faucet.
ideas.why: The wheel pays the same on day 1 and day 100, so the returning player's reward is identical to a stranger's.

ideas.title: Wheel risk choice
ideas.body: Before spinning, the member picks between two boards: the standard board with steady small prizes, or the long-shot board that is mostly nothing with occasional large XP and scrip, both published with their weights and both holding the same expected value. The chosen board is recorded with the spin, and the boards' composition rotates each season. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: two boards with identical expected value still feel rigged if only one is reported on, so the history page must show observed results for both boards or the choice only adds distrust.
ideas.why: The wheel is the same 30-second ritual every day, and a single choice before the spin gives it a decision.

ideas.title: Earned bonus wheel spins
ideas.body: A member earns at most one extra spin per day by completing an arcade objective after the daily spin (win three rounds of any game), plus one more for a successful heist; extra spins use a reduced prize table and are stored as vouchers on the progress row so they cannot be claimed twice. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: extra spins on the full table multiply the daily faucet, so the reduced table and the hard cap of two extra spins a day are the whole safety mechanism.
ideas.why: The wheel is the arcade's strongest return hook and currently ends the moment the single spin is spent.

ideas.title: Press-your-luck daily claim
ideas.body: The daily login bonus becomes a choice: take today's amount, or defer it and double it tomorrow - but deferring loses the day if tomorrow's claim is missed, and only the most recent day can ever be deferred. The decision is stored with the claim date and the doubling is shown before the choice is made, so the gamble is explicit. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a doubling that can be stacked becomes an exponential faucet, so only one deferred day may exist at a time and a late claim must decay rather than pay.
ideas.why: The login bonus is a button that everyone presses without thinking, and a single decision makes the daily ritual a choice.

ideas.title: Daily loop completion bonus
ideas.body: Completing the whole daily loop - claim the login bonus, spin the wheel, play one round - grants a small completion bonus and advances a loop streak tracked separately from both the login streak and the game streak. The dashboard card shows the three steps checked from the existing progress fields, and the bonus scales modestly with the loop streak up to a cap. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a third streak counter beside login and game streaks becomes noise nobody can keep straight, so the card must show all three in one place or the feature adds confusion instead of habit.
ideas.why: The three daily actions happen in three different places, and nothing currently rewards doing all of them.

ideas.title: Crew heist raid
ideas.body: Three to five members raid one target in a timed window: each pays the attempt cost, the engine resolves the raid as one combined heist whose chance scales with the participants' combined level difference against the target, and the take splits by contribution while the target's normal defence applies once. The victim sees a single raid notification rather than a burst of pings. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: a group raid multiplies exactly the pressure the per-victim flood check exists to limit, so the raid must count against every participant's hourly cap and against a global daily cap on the target.
ideas.why: Stealing is currently a lone act, and the crews and fleets the site already has give members a natural group to raid with.

ideas.title: Heist bait and trace
ideas.body: A member marks part of their balance as bait; if a heist against them succeeds that day the bait amount is flagged and the thief carries a visible 'traced' marker for 24 hours, during which their own heists succeed less often. The bait is disclosed to no one in advance, so it is a trap the victim sets, and the marker clears on the timer rather than by paying it off. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: an invisible defence that punishes thieves at random reads as unfair, so the trace must be announced to the thief when it fires with its reason and duration.
ideas.why: The steal settings let a member choose a price but give them no way to do anything active about being targeted.

ideas.title: Counter-heist revenge window
ideas.body: A robbed member gets one boosted counter-attempt against that thief within 24 hours, with the success bonus computed from the amount taken and the attempt free when the thief sits above the victim's level bracket. The window is single-use, recorded against the original heist row, and expires silently. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a free boosted hit makes robbing the strong a bad idea for the wrong reason, so the boost must taper with the stolen amount, never guarantee success, and the thief's existing per-victim flood protection must still apply.
ideas.why: A successful heist currently ends the interaction, and a single window gives the victim an answer without opening a war.
